opportunities.title: Successive same-kind batches are different instances under two removal deadlines

source.unit: Theophrastus De odoribus, complete section26, NAME=26 through next section heading
source.layer: Ancient work in cached English Loeb translation; page states first publication1926. No pre1450 witness or copying claim.

complete_content_account: Kypros manufacture resembles rose-perfume; its flowers must soon be removed and squeezed, otherwise soaking causes decay and an unpleasant smell that ruins the perfume.
Quince manufacture is similar: oil is made astringent first and is cold when quinces are introduced.
Each quince batch is taken out before blackening and before the next batch is introduced; blackening accompanies decay through thorough soaking.

owner_predicates.predicate: ASTRINGENT(o) after preparation; COLD(o) at quince insertion
owner_predicates.commitment: manufacturing description; no automatic humoral HOT/COLD or yield meaning

owner_predicates.predicate: REMOVE(b_i,o) precedes both BLACKEN(b_i) and INSERT(b_next,o)
owner_predicates.commitment: instruction over successive batches, not an assertion that every actual batch was successfully removed

owner_predicates.owner: kypros flowers f and perfume p
owner_predicates.predicate: delayed removal permits soaking-caused DECAY(f), BAD_SMELL(p) and RUIN(p)
owner_predicates.commitment: source causal conditional; not a biconditional guarantee against every other source of spoilage

shared_grammar_offer.kind_vs_instance: KIND(b_i)=quince and KIND(b_next)=quince does not imply b_i=b_next. NEXT introduces a distinct batch instance; later removal reference selects its written batch instance rather than the kind.
shared_grammar_offer.common_reference: REF(id) returns a previously written participant with unchanged sort. It creates no fresh object; INTRO(kind,id) creates a participant of that kind. Common reference can serve oil and ingredient objects without making them identical.
shared_grammar_offer.common_time: BEFORE(event1,event2) contributes one strict event order reused for removal versus blackening and removal versus next insertion; neither required order contains the other.
shared_grammar_offer.common_clause: PRED(owner,arguments) states a property or relation; MUST(PRED) retains instruction force and IF(delay,PRED) retains conditional force. These wrappers cannot donate the ingredient, action or owner.
shared_grammar_offer.whole_residuals: Any prospective whole residual distinguishes instruction, conditional, next-batch binding or exact entry context. A residual containing the whole oil/batch/deadline assertion would defeat effective reuse.
shared_grammar_offer.surface_licenses: UNBOUND: no target whole or substring is assigned REF, INTRO, BEFORE, MUST, IF or any noun. Formal aN constraints do not identify any of these meanings.

independently_changing_consequences: A remove-after-next account violates the successor-order instruction even if the first batch has not blackened.
A remove-after-blackening account violates the deterioration deadline even if no next batch was inserted yet.

An accumulation account has two same-kind batches present together; the replacement instruction has the previous batch removed before successor insertion. Generic quince-kind identity cannot erase that difference.
retained_uncertainties: Continuing identity of oil o across replacements is a declared process inference, not an explicit SAME-OIL clause in the source.
Kypros squeezing is not transferred to quince without a separate written commitment.
No number of batches, fixed dwell duration, guaranteed preservation or achieved product is stated.
Rose-perfume is an external comparison; complete section26 is not a complete reconstruction of the referenced rose procedure.

opportunities.title: A repeated astronomical phase governs plant state within an explicit life-stage scope

source.layer: Cached electronic ancient Latin edition; no medieval donor date, manuscript collation, species identification or Latin-default claim.

complete_content_account: 107 changes from the preceding tree to a same-named Egyptian marsh herb after Nile retreat, and compares stem/leaves with bean, head with poppy and grains with millet.

108 inhabitants heap heads for putrefaction, wash-separate, dry and pound grains for bread. A separate reported natural-state account closes/covers the heads at sunset and opens them at sunrise, until ripening and white-flower fall.
109 separately reports the Euphrates head and flower submerging in evening until midnight, then rising gradually, emerging and opening at sunrise, and rising well above water.
110 gives quince-sized root, black rind, white interior, raw/water-cooked/ember-cooked food and pig fattening on its waste. The waste is not specifically identified as head-to-bread residue.

owner_predicates.owner: Egyptian reported head carrier h at chosen declared granularity
owner_predicates.predicate: SUNSET(t) guards CLOSED(h,t) and COVERED_BY(h,leaves,t); SUNRISE(t) guards OPEN(h,t)
owner_predicates.commitment: reported recurring state within stated life-stage interval; no arbitrary replacement of h at each predicate

owner_predicates.owner: the scoped narrated carrier and white flower
owner_predicates.predicate: recurrence description extends to RIPEN and FLOWER_FALL boundary
owner_predicates.commitment: bounds the narration; does not assert universal perpetual closure afterward

owner_predicates.predicate: SUBMERGED through midnight, later RISING and EMERGED at sunrise
owner_predicates.commitment: separate locality/report; not inherited by every Egyptian specimen

owner_predicates.predicate: bread processing attaches to head/grain; root food and following waste account retain a distinct part owner
owner_predicates.commitment: same plant kind does not identify these parts or their products

shared_grammar_offer.common_reference: REF(id) preserves a written head/part identity; PART_OF(part,plant) does not identify two parts. Generic kind repetition cannot serve as same-specimen reference.
shared_grammar_offer.common_phase_guard: WHEN(phase(t),PRED(owner,t)) uses the same owner/time interface for sunset closed/covered and sunrise open; paid residuals select phase and state rather than encoding the entire conjunction.
shared_grammar_offer.common_conjunction: AND joins the paired closed/covered states and joins maturity/flower-fall boundary content. Dropping either conjunct changes the reported content.
shared_grammar_offer.common_scope: UNTIL(boundary,description) restricts the narrated recurrence to its stated interval. No NOT-OPEN after endpoint is silently added; a strict cessation law requires its own declared C0 cost.
shared_grammar_offer.common_attribution: REPORT(location,description) separates Egyptian and Euphrates natural-state accounts from inhabitants processing heads.
shared_grammar_offer.surface_licenses: UNBOUND: no Voynich form is assigned WHEN, UNTIL, AND, REPORT, PART_OF, OPEN, SUNRISE or any noun. No inherited chey, chor/shor or luminary-name value.

independently_changing_consequences: Exchange the same carrier sunrise/sunset guard while retaining state meanings: opening and closing now occur at the wrong source phase.
Retain phase/state relation but omit flower fall or ripening: the supplied boundary loses one actual source conjunct.
Extend Euphrates submergence to Egyptian specimens or head bread-residue to root waste: owner/report scope changes despite shared plant kind.
A later new head of the same kind is compatible with the source. Its new generation neither proves survival of the earlier head nor violates an unstated never-open-again rule.
retained_uncertainties: Source plural heads and flower wording does not choose single-head, group or plant-level granularity. Persistent individual identity is an authored model choice.
The until phrase does not independently entail a strict per-instance cessation equation, plant death, no new generation or no later opening.
Maturity and flower fall have stated endpoint scope; their detailed mutual temporal order is not supplied.
Pig-fattening waste follows the root account and is not explicitly waste from bread processing.
